title: Perf Canary Internal Sync - baseline, rollout plan, alert payload (Runtime/SRE/Telemetry)
summary: Cross-team internal sync to align on perf-regression canary baseline strategy, phased rollout plan (us-east first), and what context must be attached to alerts to reduce time-to-triage. Runtime wants attribution across runtime_build/scheduler_mode/kernel selection without blowing up metric cardinality; Telemetry wants a stable label schema with a hard budget; SRE wants paging hygiene (deploy-window suppression, minimum sample sizes, and clear severity mapping). Agreed to v1 baseline as rolling 7-day median per slice with a pinned known-good fallback during major releases, plus deploy annotation-based suppression and warmup exclusion. Alert payload will include direct links to dashboards, last deploy annotation, runtime SHA, GPU SKU, scheduler mode, kernel id/fallback reason, and batch stats.
topics: Baseline strategy: rolling median vs pinned known-good, and how to handle deploy windows
Rollout phases: us-east limited models, then expand to eu-west and more GPU SKUs
Metric definitions and label schema; cardinality controls
Alert policy: paging vs ticketing, grouping/dedup keys, maintenance windows
Alert payload fields for fast triage (runtime build, kernel selection, scheduler mode, batch stats)
Noise reduction: warmup, cache priming, outlier handling
next_steps: Nadia to circulate final v1 metric spec and allowed label list (with examples) to Runtime + SRE by EOW
Rafael to propose PagerDuty dedup/grouping keys and severity mapping for review
Omar to confirm runtime emits runtime_build + scheduler_mode + kernel_id/fallback_reason gated on source=perf-canary
Connor to confirm deploy annotation events include runtime_version and git_sha and land in dashboards
Sean to draft maintenance window/suppression guidelines and add to runbook
Noah/Sofia to decide which scheduler settings are pinned for canary to reduce variance in phase 1
action_items: Nadia Rahman - Share label schema proposal (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, request_mode) and cardinality budget notes - Due 2026-01-16
Rafael Mendes - Draft alert routing + dedup keys (page SRE first, auto-assign Runtime after confirmation) - Due 2026-01-20
Omar El-Sayed - Validate canary-tag gating for kernel-selection debug export and batch stats emission - Due 2026-01-21
Connor O'Brien - Confirm deploy-annotation pipeline end-to-end (runtime_version, git_sha) and provide Grafana annotation query - Due 2026-01-21
Sean Gallagher - Write deploy-window suppression and false-positive checklist for runbook - Due 2026-01-22
transcript:
Meeting: Perf Canary Internal Sync - baseline, rollout plan, alert payload (Runtime/SRE/Telemetry)
Recorded: 2026-01-15 17:00 UTC
Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Talia Benson, Noah Patel, Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed, Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Allison Grant, Connor O'Brien

[00:00] Talia Benson: Alright, we’re at time. This is the cross-team sync for the perf regression canary. Goal today is to align on three things: baseline strategy, rollout plan, and what the alert payload needs so oncall can actually do something.

[00:12] Talia Benson: Quick check, does anyone need context? This is internal only, v1 is detection and operational readiness, not a customer feature.

[00:21] Sean Gallagher: Yeah, all good.

[00:23] Logan Wright: Good.

[00:24] Noah Patel: Yep.

[00:26] Talia Benson: Cool. I’ll drive but I want Runtime, SRE, Telemetry to disagree loudly now, not during paging.

[00:37] Talia Benson: Let’s start with baseline. The proposal in the notes was “rolling 7-day median” per slice, plus a pinned known-good option for major runtime releases. Noah, can you say what you need here?

[00:52] Noah Patel: Sure. The thing we’re trying to avoid is two failure modes. One is: we roll out a regression slowly, and the baseline chases it, and we never alert. The other is: we do pinned baseline and then the world changes, new GPUs, different queueing, and we page constantly.

[01:10] Noah Patel: So I’m in favor of rolling median as primary. But I want a way to pin to a known-good runtime build during release candidates, because we do get kernel auto-tune drift and scheduler heuristic changes that look like “new normal” but are actually worse.

[01:27] Sofia Ivanova: And also, scheduler changes can change batching distribution. Your median can shift not because the kernel got slower, but because you’re forming different batch sizes. So the baseline has to be slice-aware enough.

[01:40] Nadia Rahman: When you say slice-aware, we need to be really careful. If you want “model x region x gpu_sku x runtime_build x scheduler_mode x kernel_id” as labels, that’s basically not going to work in the metrics pipeline.

[01:54] Allison Grant: Yeah, cardinality will explode. We need a strict label allowlist. Kernel id should not be a metric label in v1, in my opinion.

[02:03] Omar El-Sayed: Kernel id can be attached as exemplars or in traces, but I don’t want it as a label either. We can include it in the alert payload by querying a recent trace or a log line for canary-tagged requests.

[02:17] Logan Wright: Exactly. For baseline computation we need stable time series. The time series should be at like: model, region, gpu_sku, request_mode. Maybe scheduler_mode. runtime_build only if you’re okay with it being sparse.

[02:31] Sean Gallagher: From oncall’s perspective, if it pages and the payload doesn’t say “this correlates with runtime deploy X,” we lose a ton of time. So I want runtime_build in the alert context, but I don’t necessarily need it as a dimension on the chart.

[02:46] Connor O'Brien: On deploy annotations: we can annotate dashboards with runtime_version and git_sha. That’s already in the release metadata event stream, we just have to make sure it gets into the observability pack. There was some mismatch in staging previously.

[03:01] Talia Benson: So let’s separate: baseline computation dimensions versus alert enrichment dimensions. Nadia, what’s the max we can afford for baseline series?

[03:11] Nadia Rahman: For v1, I’d say allowed labels for canary aggregate metrics: model, region, gpu_sku, request_mode. We can add scheduler_mode if it’s low cardinality, like “default” vs “pinned.” But no per-kernel id, no per-prompt id as labels.

[03:30] Nadia Rahman: If we need prompt shapes, we can do a small enumerated set like “shape_a, shape_b,” not arbitrary IDs.

[03:38] Sofia Ivanova: That’s okay. For scheduler pinning, we’re talking one toggle: disable experimental heuristic X, and we label that scheduler_mode=pinned. So two values.

[03:49] Noah Patel: Works for me. Kernel id stays out of metrics labels. But I want it in the payload when it fires.

[04:00] Omar El-Sayed: We can do that by having the runtime emit a “kernel selection dump” only when source=perf-canary, and we attach it to the trace span. Then the alert includes a link to a trace explorer query.

[04:14] Sean Gallagher: Okay, but I want the alert to be actionable without having to click through five systems. If the kernel dump is crucial, include the selected kernel id and fallback reason as text in the payload too.

[04:27] Omar El-Sayed: That’s fair. We can put “kernel_id=…” and “fallback_reason=…” in the alert. But it needs to be rate-limited.

[04:38] Logan Wright: The alerting pipeline can also snapshot “recent exemplars” from the metric stream, but that’s more work. Simpler is: detector includes fields it already has: last runtime deploy annotation, and then it can fetch one recent trace for that slice.

[04:55] Talia Benson: Let’s park the “fetch trace automatically” as nice-to-have. For v1, we’ll manually click from the alert.

[05:04] Talia Benson: Back to baseline strategy. Sean, what do you need for paging hygiene?

[05:11] Sean Gallagher: Minimum sample size and a suppression policy. If we’re computing p95 latency and tokens/sec, those can be noisy. We need something like: don’t evaluate until N canary runs in window, exclude warmup, and suppress during deploy windows.

[05:29] Sean Gallagher: Also severity mapping: small regression should ticket, big regression pages. And dedup keys so we don’t get one page per model per region per GPU every 2 minutes.

[05:42] Rafael Mendes: +1. I want grouping like: “model+region+gpu_sku+request_mode” is the group key. And then within that we can include both metrics in one incident: p95 and tokens/sec.

[05:56] Allison Grant: Please do not group across regions. That tends to hide regional issues.

[06:01] Rafael Mendes: Agreed, region stays in the key.

[06:05] Nadia Rahman: On sample size: we should define the evaluation windows. I’ve seen folks do 10-minute windows with rolling evaluation every minute, but that’s overkill. We can do 15 minutes evaluation with a 1 hour lookback for baseline? Or baseline is 7 days.

[06:22] Logan Wright: Baseline is separate from evaluation window. Think: “current window” maybe 30 minutes for stability, and baseline is median of prior 7 days for the same time-of-day? Or just global 7-day median.

[06:37] Noah Patel: Time-of-day matters for contention. If canary is isolated, maybe less. But if it’s in the same fleet, you’ll see diurnal patterns.

[06:47] Sofia Ivanova: Canary is “canary-safe” class, low priority. It still shares GPUs though, right? So diurnal can matter.

[06:55] Omar El-Sayed: It shares nodes unless we buy dedicated nodes, which we’re not doing v1.

[07:00] Talia Benson: So what’s the compromise? Logan?

[07:04] Logan Wright: For v1: baseline is rolling 7-day median per slice, not time-of-day segmented. We mitigate diurnal by making canary run frequently and using median, plus outlier filtering. If it’s still noisy, we adjust windows or add an hour-of-day baseline later.

[07:25] Sean Gallagher: I’m okay with that if we have deploy-window suppression, because deploys are the biggest false-positive generator.

[07:32] Connor O'Brien: Deploy windows: we can mark start/end for region rollout. But we need to define “deploy window.” Is it the 30 minutes around the annotation? Or the time it takes to roll across the region.

[07:46] Sean Gallagher: For paging, I want a maintenance window mechanism that can be set when release train is rolling. At minimum, auto-suppress for, say, 45 minutes after a runtime deploy annotation in that region.

[08:02] Nadia Rahman: That needs to be very explicit, otherwise people will use suppression to hide regressions.

[08:06] Allison Grant: We should log when suppression is active and show it on dashboards.

[08:11] Talia Benson: Yep. “Suppression is visible” is a requirement.

[08:16] Noah Patel: Also, suppression shouldn’t block detection entirely; it can downgrade to ticketing. Like, during deploy we still want a signal, just not a page.

[08:28] Sean Gallagher: Exactly. During known deploy windows, create a ticket and post to a channel, don’t page.

[08:35] Rafael Mendes: For PagerDuty, we can route “non-page” as event to incident-bot only. Or we can create a low urgency service. We need to choose.

[08:45] Talia Benson: Let’s do: in suppression window, no PD. Just incident-bot + Jira ticket. Outside suppression window, PD page for Sev2 thresholds.

[08:56] Sean Gallagher: Works.

[08:58] Talia Benson: Okay. Next: rollout plan. Phase 1 is us-east limited models. Sofia, what’s the plan for pinning scheduler settings to reduce variance?

[09:09] Sofia Ivanova: We can pin canary requests to a specific scheduler config profile. The main thing is disabling the new heuristic that reorders decode vs prefill when the queue is mixed. It helps customer workloads but creates variance in tokens/sec measurement.

[09:27] Sofia Ivanova: For canary, we set scheduler_mode=pinned and we run both streaming and non-streaming. That isolates regressions from heuristic drift.

[09:36] Noah Patel: Just to be clear, we’re okay measuring something slightly less “real” if it’s stable and catches regressions early.

[09:46] Sean Gallagher: I’m fine with synthetic stability as long as we understand it’s a canary, not SLO.

[09:52] Logan Wright: We can also have two canaries later: “stable mode” and “realistic mode.” But v1 should be stable.

[10:00] Talia Benson: Great. Which models in phase 1?

[10:05] Noah Patel: I propose 2 to 3 models. One that’s decoder-heavy, one that’s prefill-heavy. Like a 7B-ish and a bigger one.

[10:15] Omar El-Sayed: The runner already supports a model list and prompt sets. We should pick ones that have steady traffic and are in both us-east and eu-west.

[10:26] Nadia Rahman: And please, please keep the prompt shapes small and enumerated. Like two shapes per model: short prefill/long decode and long prefill/short decode.

[10:38] Talia Benson: Okay. So phase 1: us-east, 2-3 models, two prompt shapes, streaming and non-streaming, scheduler_mode pinned. Then phase 2 expand to eu-west and more models.

[10:55] Connor O'Brien: We also need to confirm the deploy annotation is regional. If a global deploy touches us-east first, annotation needs “region=us-east” or else dashboards will look weird.

[11:06] Logan Wright: We can include region label on the annotation event. I’ll double-check the event schema.

[11:12] Talia Benson: Good. Now the big one: alert payload fields. Sean, what do you want in the PD page?

[11:20] Sean Gallagher: In the PD page: what is regressing (p95 latency or tokens/sec), by how much, current value, baseline value, evaluation window, and the slice: model, region, gpu_sku, request_mode, scheduler_mode.

[11:39] Sean Gallagher: Then links: Grafana dashboard filtered to that slice, runbook link, and “last deploy annotation” link or at least timestamp + runtime_version + git_sha. If we can include “recent PRs” link, great, but not required.

[11:56] Rafael Mendes: Also a dedup key visible in the alert. Helps with debugging routing.

[12:02] Omar El-Sayed: Runtime context: runtime_build, runtime_version, git_sha, kernel_id, fallback_reason, batch stats. At least for one representative canary request around the time.

[12:14] Nadia Rahman: Batch stats as what exactly?

[12:17] Omar El-Sayed: Like: batch_size, number_of_prefills, number_of_decodes, max_seq_len_in_batch, and maybe queue_wait_ms.

[12:28] Sofia Ivanova: Queue wait is huge. Often regressions are “scheduler got weird” not kernel slow.

[12:33] Noah Patel: Also KV cache hit/miss? At least “cache_enabled” and “prefix_cache_hit_rate” if we have it.

[12:42] Logan Wright: Cache hit rate as a metric label is a no. But you can include it as a numeric field in payload. Or show it on dashboard.

[12:51] Allison Grant: Right, payload can have numbers, that’s not cardinality. But make sure we don’t attach a huge JSON blob.

[12:58] Sean Gallagher: Keep it to like 10-15 fields, not 100.

[13:02] Talia Benson: Let’s enumerate v1 payload fields. I’m going to read back what I heard:

[13:08] Talia Benson: Required: model, region, gpu_sku, request_mode (streaming vs non), scheduler_mode. Metric: p95 latency delta percent, current p95, baseline p95, tokens/sec delta percent, current tokens/sec, baseline tokens/sec. Time window and sample size.

[13:32] Talia Benson: Context: last deploy timestamp, runtime_version, git_sha. Runtime_build if that’s different from runtime_version.

[13:41] Talia Benson: Debug hints: kernel_id, fallback_reason, batch_size, max_seq_len, queue_wait_ms.

[13:49] Talia Benson: Links: Grafana dashboard with filters, runbook, and maybe a trace search link.

[13:58] Rafael Mendes: That’s good.

[13:59] Logan Wright: Works.

[14:01] Nadia Rahman: Works, but sample size must be explicit. If we evaluate with 12 samples and page, that’s a problem.

[14:10] Sean Gallagher: Minimum sample size: I want 50 requests in window for page, maybe 20 for ticket.

[14:18] Noah Patel: Depends on cadence. How often are we running canary per model? Every minute?

[14:23] Omar El-Sayed: We can do every 30 seconds per model for a given region, but that’s a lot. We might do every 2 minutes per model per mode.

[14:34] Logan Wright: The overhead is not just traffic, it’s metric emission. But okay.

[14:39] Talia Benson: Let’s not settle cadence in this call. But we need sample size thresholds that match realistic cadence.

[14:46] Nadia Rahman: I’ll propose: evaluation window 30 minutes, page requires at least 60 samples, ticket requires at least 20. If cadence is too low, we don’t evaluate.

[14:59] Sean Gallagher: Fine for now.

[15:01] Sofia Ivanova: Also warmup exclusion. First N requests after process start or deploy should not be counted.

[15:08] Omar El-Sayed: Runner can do warmup runs that are not emitted to metrics. We already have a “warmup=true” tag internally.

[15:16] Logan Wright: As long as warmup is excluded from the metrics time series, okay.

[15:20] Allison Grant: Add it to spec. “Warmup requests must not emit perf_canary p95/tps samples.”

[15:27] Talia Benson: Great. Now, label schema and cardinality. Nadia/Allison, can we align on what labels we allow, so Runtime doesn’t add new ones in PR review later?

[15:39] Nadia Rahman: Yes. I want a hard allowlist:
- model
- region
- gpu_sku
- request_mode
- scheduler_mode
And optionally “deployment_mode” if we need hosted vs dedicated, but for now it’s internal canary so it’s fine.

[16:02] Nadia Rahman: Not allowed as labels: runtime_build, git_sha, prompt_text, prompt_id, kernel_id, customer_id, route, pod.

[16:13] Omar El-Sayed: runtime_build not allowed as label is okay, but we still want it on dashboards. We’ll do dashboard annotations plus include it in payload.

[16:23] Logan Wright: We can also have a separate “deploy info” metric that’s basically an event stream, not a time series. That’s what Connor is doing.

[16:33] Connor O'Brien: Yep, it’s an annotation event. We’ll ensure it includes runtime_version and git_sha.

[16:39] Sean Gallagher: Just don’t let deploy annotations lag by 30 minutes. That’s when it’s useless.

[16:45] Connor O'Brien: Understood. We’ll validate latency.

[16:49] Talia Benson: Cool. Now thresholds. We don’t need final numbers today, but we do need initial guidance. Sean, what do you consider a page-worthy regression?

[16:59] Sean Gallagher: For phase 1, I’d be conservative. Page if p95 latency regresses by more than 15% for 2 consecutive windows, and tokens/sec drops more than 20%. Ticket if smaller.

[17:15] Noah Patel: I’d do something like 10% for p95 for certain models. But sure, phase 1 conservative is okay.

[17:23] Sofia Ivanova: Tokens/sec is very sensitive to scheduling. If we pin scheduler, 20% is reasonable.

[17:30] Logan Wright: The detector can be symmetric: alert on improvement too? Sometimes improvement indicates metric bug.

[17:37] Sean Gallagher: Ticket on improvement, don’t page. And only if it’s huge.

[17:43] Nadia Rahman: Also watch for p95 window mismatch bugs. We saw that in other projects: runtime uses 10-minute bucket, telemetry uses 5-minute.

[17:52] Omar El-Sayed: We should put in a validation doc. Compare runtime logs vs aggregated metrics for one day.

[17:58] Talia Benson: That exists as a working doc; Logan and Nadia are tracking it.

[18:03] Logan Wright: Yep. We already have a few missing label cases to fix.

[18:08] Talia Benson: Great. Now, debate: should baseline be “last 7 days median” or “pinned known-good” in phase 1?

[18:16] Noah Patel: Rolling 7-day median. Pinned is too brittle for the first rollout.

[18:22] Sean Gallagher: Agree. Pinned baseline is great when you have a stable known-good. We don’t yet.

[18:27] Allison Grant: The ADR should capture that pinned is a fallback, not default.

[18:33] Talia Benson: Okay. We’ll write it as: default rolling 7-day median baseline; pinned baseline for RC comparisons and investigations.

[18:43] Rafael Mendes: And when pinned baseline is active, how do we indicate that in the alert? So oncall knows it’s not the normal mode.

[18:50] Logan Wright: Add “baseline_mode=rolling|pinned” as a field in alert payload, not a metric label.

[18:56] Sean Gallagher: +1.

[18:58] Talia Benson: Good.

[19:01] Talia Benson: Last piece: who gets paged and when. SRE wants first page, then runtime. Sean, can you outline the flow?

[19:09] Sean Gallagher: Page hits SRE oncall. They do initial quality check: is it a single GPU SKU node, is sample size sufficient, is suppression active, do we see correlation to deploy annotation. If signal is real, they reassign or tag Runtime oncall.

[19:27] Noah Patel: Runtime wants to be pulled in quickly if it’s correlated with a runtime deploy or kernel change.

[19:33] Sean Gallagher: Sure, payload includes “deploy correlation likely” or “last deploy within 60 minutes.” That can trigger auto-CC to Runtime even if SRE is primary.

[19:45] Rafael Mendes: We can implement that as: PD page goes to SRE only, but incident-bot posts in #eng-oncall and tags @runtime-oncall if deploy correlation is within X.

[19:58] Omar El-Sayed: That’s good. It avoids two pages but still pulls Runtime.

[20:03] Talia Benson: Great.

[20:05] Talia Benson: I’m going to open it up for anything we missed.

[20:10] Nadia Rahman: One more thing: p95 definition. Are we measuring request latency end-to-end, or time-to-first-token for streaming, or both?

[20:18] Omar El-Sayed: The canary will emit both. But the primary p95 we alert on should be end-to-end latency for non-streaming and time-to-first-token for streaming. Tokens/sec is separate.

[20:31] Logan Wright: We need to be explicit in naming. Like “latency_ms_p95” for non-streaming and “ttft_ms_p95” for streaming.

[20:40] Allison Grant: And do not label it with “metric_type.” Just separate metric names.

[20:46] Nadia Rahman: Yes, separate metrics.

[20:49] Sean Gallagher: Oncall wants them combined in one page though, right? Like if streaming TTFT regresses but non-streaming doesn’t, that’s a clue.

[20:58] Rafael Mendes: We can include both values in the same alert payload for that slice.

[21:03] Talia Benson: Great. Another thing: outlier handling. If one node is contended, p95 jumps. Are we filtering outliers?

[21:12] Logan Wright: For canary, we can do simple outlier filtering at sample level, like clamp crazy high values or drop top 1% before computing p95. But then it’s not p95.

[21:23] Noah Patel: Please don’t do that. We should keep p95 as a real p95. Better approach is to reduce variance: pin scheduler, warmup exclusion, and maybe detect node-level outliers and annotate them rather than filter.

[21:37] Sofia Ivanova: We can also tag node_id in traces, not in metrics, so you can see if it’s one bad node.

[21:45] Sean Gallagher: I’m aligned. No hidden filtering. If we need outlier handling, it should be explicit and documented.

[21:52] Allison Grant: Put it in runbook: “check if regression is isolated to one GPU host” with steps.

[21:59] Talia Benson: Good.

[22:01] Talia Benson: Anything else? Connor, deploy annotation concerns?

[22:06] Connor O'Brien: Just that runtime_version vs runtime_build naming is inconsistent across teams. We should standardize the field names in the payload: runtime_version (human), git_sha (full or short), and build_id (CI build).

[22:22] Omar El-Sayed: Runtime uses runtime_build as a string. We can map it to build_id in the alert.

[22:29] Logan Wright: Telemetry will pass through what you emit; just don’t add it as label.

[22:35] Sean Gallagher: In the page, short sha is fine, but include full sha in the dashboard link query.

[22:41] Rafael Mendes: Noted.

[22:43] Talia Benson: Okay. I think we have alignment.

[22:47] Talia Benson: I’ll recap decisions and next steps.

[22:51] Talia Benson: Decisions:
1) Baseline mode v1 is rolling 7-day median per slice. Pinned known-good baseline is supported as an investigation / RC mode, not default.
2) Canary metric label allowlist for aggregate time series: model, region, gpu_sku, request_mode, scheduler_mode. No runtime_build/git_sha/kernel_id/prompt_id labels.
3) Deploy-window handling: auto-suppress paging for a window after deploy annotation; during suppression, create ticket + post to channel, no PD page.
4) Phase 1 rollout: us-east, 2-3 models, two prompt shapes, streaming + non-streaming, scheduler_mode pinned.
5) Alert payload must include: deltas and absolutes for p95 (latency or TTFT depending on mode) and tokens/sec, sample size, baseline_mode, last deploy info (runtime_version, git_sha), plus debug hints (kernel_id/fallback_reason, batch stats, queue wait), and links (dashboard, runbook, optional trace query).

[23:36] Talia Benson: Next steps are in the action items list; Nadia will circulate spec, Rafael will propose routing/dedup keys, Omar will validate runtime emits gated debug fields, Connor will confirm annotation pipeline.

[23:51] Sean Gallagher: One more small thing. Can we add a note that this is not Datadog-based; it’s Grafana + our internal stack, because people keep asking “where is it in Datadog.”

[24:00] Logan Wright: Yeah, we can add that to the announcement when phase 1 launches.

[24:05] Talia Benson: Great point.

[24:08] Talia Benson: Alright, thanks everyone. I’ll send notes.

[24:12] (Some crosstalk)

[24:14] Meeting ended (recording continues briefly)

[24:18] Speaker 2: okay.

[24:20] Recording stopped.
